title: Part of a Survivor Overpayment Left for Offset Against Continuing Income Annuities Payments
content:
When a surviving payee on an Ashgrove Income Annuities joint contract (status survivor continuing) settles an overpayment directly, part of it may be left to be recovered by offset from the survivor's own payments; the payee repays now the overpayment owed less that part. The part left for offset is:

1. **An installment held for the surviving payee for a payment date after the first death.** When the installment held in suspense for the latest held payment date falls after the first death, the part is the tier's overpayment offset maximum percentage (25%) of the survivor percentage of that held installment — the survivor percentage of the held installment rounded to the cent, and 25% of that rounded to the cent — never more than the overpayment.
2. **Nothing held, next installment within 10 days.** When nothing is held and the survivor's next installment falls due within the cutoff of **10** days (counted from today to the next payment date on the contract), the part is 25% of the survivor installment now on the contract, rounded to the cent, never more than the overpayment.

Where neither describes the contract, neither applies.

### Worked cases (hypothetical Joint 50% Survivor contract, overpayment owed $1,350.00)

| Held for a payment date after the first death | Days to the survivor's next installment | Part left for offset | Repaid now |
|---|---|---|---|
| $3,000.00 held | Any | 50% of $3,000.00 is $1,500.00; 25% of that is $375.00 | $975.00 |
| Nothing held | 10 (survivor installment $1,500.00) | 25% of $1,500.00 is $375.00 | $975.00 |
| Nothing held | 11 | Neither applies | — |

With an overpayment owed of only $200.00 and $3,000.00 held, the part left for offset is $200.00, because it is never more than the overpayment, and nothing is repaid now.
